CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left arm pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is an elderly male presenting with left arm pain that started approximately two weeks ago. He woke at 2:00 AM with severe arm pain. He applied ice which provided some relief. He attempted to improve circulation by holding his arm down but found this ineffective. Pain resolved around 4-5 AM and he was able to return to sleep. This pattern of nighttime pain recurred over several nights. He was subsequently evaluated by another physician who suspected a pinched nerve. Patient reports pain starts in the hand and radiates down the entire arm. He notes weakness in his hand, particularly with gripping. He reports one finger has not functioned properly since a previous injury. A previous physician prescribed numbing medicine, a neck pill, and gabapentin, which has provided some relief. Since starting treatment, nighttime symptoms have improved significantly. However, his hand continues to bother him during the day, particularly if symptoms occurred the preceding night. He denies neck or shoulder discomfort with movement.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies neck pain with head turning or shoulder movement. He notes mild strain in the neck with head turning. He reports weakness and numbness in the left hand and arm.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Cervical arthritis with disc degeneration.
Peripheral neuropathy (lower extremities, rated as 1% VA disability).
History of finger injury with residual dysfunction.

MEDICATIONS
Gabapentin (dose to be confirmed).
Numbing medicine.
Eliquis.
Neck pill (unspecified).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a Veteran with 1% disability rating related to lower extremity neuropathy. Patient uses a wheelchair for mobility.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Elderly white male in wheelchair, no apparent distress.
Cervical spine: Non-tender over cervical spine. Mildly restricted cervical extension. Right and left lateral rotation symmetric with mild lateral neck pain but no radicular pain.
Neurologic: Bilateral biceps, triceps, and brachioradialis reflexes 1+ bilaterally. Sensation intact. Strength preserved. Spurling's maneuver benign.
Extremities: Hand strength adequate with good grip bilaterally.

RESULTS
Cervical X-ray: Significant disc degeneration at C5-C6 and to a lesser extent at C4-C5 and C3-C4. Significant lower cervical facet arthropathy at C6-C7 and C7-T1. C7-T1 level difficult to visualize on current films.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Left upper extremity neuropathy suspicious for cervical radiculopathy with possible contribution of peripheral neuropathy. Plan: Order cervical MRI to identify exact location of nerve root compression. Tentatively plan left C7-T1 epidural steroid injection pending MRI results. Continue home exercise program. Continue gabapentin twice daily. Follow up after procedure to assess symptom relief. Patient denies use of blood thinners.

2. Neck pain in the setting of cervical arthritis and disc degeneration. Plan: Continue current management as above.
